title: One Element, Six Oxidation States: Why Transition Metals Vary
subject: Chemistry
objective: The ns and (n−1)d electrons of a transition metal are close in energy, so both can take part in bonding. Manganese (3d⁵ 4s²) shows every state from +2 to +7; the most states occur in the middle of the series, Sc shows only +3 and Zn only +2, and the states change in steps of one.

fill.q: Transition metals show variable oxidation states because the ns and (n−1)____ electrons are close in energy.
Manganese shows oxidation states from +2 to +____.
The oxidation state of Mn in KMnO₄ is +____.
Zinc shows only the +____ oxidation state.

tf.q: The most oxidation states occur in the middle of the 3d series.
Oxidation states of transition elements usually differ by one.

ar.a: Manganese shows oxidation states from +2 to +7.
ar.r: Both its 4s and 3d electrons can take part in bonding.
Zinc has the largest atomic radius in the 3d series.
ar.explain: A true; R false: Sc is the largest; zinc's full 3d¹⁰ is not used.

short.q: Why does the number of oxidation states rise to a maximum at Mn and then fall?
short.solution: Up to Mn more electrons (4s + 3d) are available; after Mn the d electrons pair up and fewer are used, and Zn's full d¹⁰ leaves only +2.

match.explain: Each element matches its oxidation states.
